To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sub-MIC concentrations of antibiotics can alter the outcome of ecological interactions in microbial populations by promoting the evolution of resistance.
sublethal concentrations of the antibiotic streptomyces and the lytic bacteriophages together promoted evolution of resistance.
sublethal concentrations of the antibiotic strepomycin (Sm) and lytic bacterio-phage together promote evolution of Sm resistance in the bacterium Escherichia coli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how sub-MICs can impact key ecological interactions.
how sub-MICs and bacteriophage together affect the evolution of antibiotic resistance and phage resistance.
the ecological and evolutionary effects of sub-MIC concentrations of antibiotics on bacteria–phage dynamics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of sub-MIC of antibiotics and lytic bacteriphage together can promote resistance evolution.

sub-MIC concentrations of Sm, when combined with a lytic phage, can increase the rate of resistance and cause phage extinction, which is in contrast to what is expected when MIC concentrations are used.
sublethal streptomycins (sub-Sm) concentrations and lytic phages together promote evolution of antibiotic resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sub-lethal streptomycin (SM) concentrations and lytic phage together promote evolution of resistance to SM, and that the phage resistance is enhanced by SM.
the combination of sublethal concentrations of antibiotics and bacteriophages promotes resistance evolution.
the combination of sub-MIC of antibiotics and bacteriophages can promote antibiotic resistance and phage resistance evolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sublethal concentrations of antibiotics can impact the evolution of bacteria, as well as key ecological interactions such as the phage-bacteria interactions.
antibiotic resistance evolution can occur at sub-MICs.
the sub-MIC concentrations of antibiotics that are commonly found in natural environments can have important consequences for the evolution of antibiotic resistance.
